title: A Talent That Feels Older Than You
core_idea: Some people interpret effortless affinities as echoes of past lives; whatever their origin, such gifts can be honoured as invitations rather than proof.
text: Some skills arrive slowly, through years of practice. Others seem to wake up the first time you try them. A melody your hands find without thinking. A craft that feels like coming home. In traditions that hold a belief in rebirth, people sometimes wonder whether a gift like this is an echo of another life. It's a lovely possibility to sit with, though no one can know it for certain, and it doesn't need to be proven to matter. Perhaps the more useful question is simpler. What does this ability ask of you now? Whatever its roots, it's here in this life, waiting to be used with care.
description: A reflection on gifts that feel strangely familiar, and the idea of past lives held gently as possibility rather than fact.
